newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-SOMERSET SHINE AS WICKETS TUMBLE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOMERSET SHINE AS WICKETS TUMBLE.

text.p: Fast bowler Kevin Shine routed Lancashire for just 88 but Somerset's batsmen also had their problems as 21 wickets fell on the opening day of their county championship match on Wednesday.
Shine took seven for 43 as Lancashire were all out before lunch at Taunton in just 22.1 overs.

Somerset appeared headed for a huge first innings lead, advancing to 113 for two, before Peter Martin and Glen Chapple led Lancashire's fightback with four victims each to dismiss the visitors for 189.
Lancashire were 40 for one at stumps and were facing the prospect of batting second time around without opener Jason Gallian who was forced to retire hurt.
A further 16 wickets fell at Headingley, where second-placed Gloucestershire were dismissed for 205. Yorkshire also found it hard going and were 127 for six at the close.
Opener Adrian Rollins hammered an unbeaten 151 to guide Derbyshire to 361 for seven against Hampshire at Chesterfield.
Rollins's brotwas also in form at The Oval, hitting 56 for Essex as he and opener Darren Robinson (98) steered their side 347 all out just before the close against Surrey.
An unbeaten 108 by Leicestershire captain James Whitaker carried the defending champions to 267 for seven against Middlesex at Lord's.
